newsitem.title: USA: At least a year before Taiwan exports resume -USDA.
newsitem.headline: At least a year before Taiwan exports resume -USDA.

text.p: A U.S. Agriculture Department official Friday predicted it would be more than a year before Taiwan pork exports could resume.

The Taiwan Council of Agriculture announced Thursday it was banning temporarily exports of fresh and frozen pork due to an outbreak of the deadly and highly contagious foot-and-mouth disease in its hog population.
"I think its going to be more than a year," said John Reddington, director of the dairy, livestock and poultry division at USDA's Foreign Agriculture Service.

Reddington said under international standards set by the International Office of Epizootics, Taiwan would need to have in place a system to eradicate food-and-mouth disease that included elimination of infected animals and innoculation to prevent infection.
He said once the innoculation program is in place it will take a year to be declared disease-free under the international body that sets universal scientific standards.
Reddington said there were no regulations to prevent countries from buying products once a nation was declared disease-free.
He stressed the extent of the problem is still not known and said it was possible Taiwan would try to set up foot- and-mouth free zones and export products from those areas.
